/h1: Does PDRN after microneedling smooth wrinkles around the eyes faster?
/deck: A randomised, split-face hospital trial of radiofrequency microneedling with a 0.3% polynucleotide serum on one side and saline on the other, in 29 women — read at source, appraised in full.
/definition: [PDRN](https://www.skingenetix.com/pages/pdrn-research) (polydeoxyribonucleotide, listed on labels as sodium DNA) is a purified mix of DNA fragments, mostly from salmon. Polynucleotides (PN) are the same class of DNA fragments, told apart by size: a 2025 review proposes the name PDRN for fragments under 1,500 kDa and PN for longer ones ([Marques et al., 2025](https://doi.org/10.3390/biom15010148)). In PDRN microneedling, it is applied straight after a microneedling session.
/answer: The Yogya 2022 trial is a randomised, split-face study in which 29 women had three sessions of radiofrequency microneedling, with a 0.3% polynucleotide serum on one side of the face and saline on the other. Wrinkle indentation around the eyes improved significantly within two months of the last session on the serum side; the saline side took six months.
/verdict: **Our verdict:** a careful hospital trial of microneedling with PDRN-type polynucleotides, and a clear result on speed. With the same procedure on both sides of every face, the polynucleotide side improved significantly by two months and the saline side by six; by six months they had drawn level. It is evidence for use after a clinic procedure, not for a leave-on serum.
/seo_title: Yogya 2022: Does PDRN After Microneedling Smooth Wrinkles?
/seo_description: In a randomised split-face trial of 29 women, PDRN microneedling eased wrinkles around the eyes in 2 months; microneedling with saline took 6.
/figures/0/label: Time to a significant change: serum vs saline
/figures/0/note: Wrinkle indentation around the eyes was significantly better two months after the last session and held to six months; the saline side's significant change came only at six months ([Yogya et al., 2022](https://doi.org/10.1007/s13555-022-00729-7)).
/figures/1/label: Wrinkle indentation, serum side, at 2 months
/figures/1/note: From 10.3 to 8.9 by Antera 3D imaging, against 11.2 to 10.3 (−8%) on the saline side; the difference between the sides was significant at two months (p = 0.006) and at three months. Values read from the paper's Figure 3.
/figures/2/note: With a numbing cream beforehand. No infection, pigment changes, lasting redness or scarring on either side, in women with medium to dark skin tones.
/glance/rows/0/v: Randomised split-face trial, described by its authors as double-blind: microneedling over the whole face, then the serum on one side and saline on the other, assigned at random. The women did not know which side was which.
/glance/rows/1/v: 30 Thai women enrolled and 29 completed, aged 24 to 54 (average 42.9), with medium to dark skin tones (Fitzpatrick types III to V) and fine to moderate wrinkles.
/glance/rows/2/v: A clinic serum with 0.3% polynucleotides (REVS NCFS 140HPn), applied straight after each session of radiofrequency microneedling (Sylfirm, 0.8–1.5 mm) and kept under a clear dressing for an hour.
/glance/rows/3/v: Saline on the other side of the same face, after the same microneedling. Both sides had the procedure, so the comparison isolates what the serum added.
/glance/rows/4/v: Three sessions two weeks apart, then checks at 2 weeks and 1, 2, 3 and 6 months after the last session.
/glance/rows/5/v: Antera 3D imaging for wrinkle indentation and maximum wrinkle depth, a Cutometer for elasticity (R2), and each woman's own rating of her improvement.
/glance/rows/6/v: 0.3% polynucleotides, fragments of 65–130 kDa (9 mg per 3 ml vial), stated in the methods, with 0.3% hyaluronic acid. The paper does not state where its polynucleotides come from.
/glance/rows/7/v: The Faculty of Medicine, Siriraj Hospital, Mahidol University. Companies provided the device (IDS Medical Systems Thailand) and the medications (GFN Group), and DermAesthetic Co. paid the journal's fee and English editing. The authors declared nothing to disclose.
/glance/rows/8/v: A for the procedure — randomised, split-face and instrument-measured. The serum went onto freshly microneedled skin, so the result belongs to that clinic use, not to a leave-on product on intact skin.
/measurements/chart/title: Wrinkle indentation around the eyes, visit by visit
/measurements/chart/subtitle: Antera 3D indentation score from the paper's Figure 3; lower means shallower wrinkles. Both sides had the same microneedling.
/measurements/chart/caption: Both sides improved. The polynucleotide side went from 10.3 to 8.9 by two months after the last session, a significant change that held to six months; the saline side, which started higher at 11.2, changed significantly at six months (9.5). The sides differed significantly at two months (p = 0.006) and three months (Yogya et al., 2022, Figure 3).
/media/alt: A glass pipette releasing a single pink droplet onto a rose-coloured surface
/media/body/0: Thirty Thai women with fine to moderate wrinkles had three sessions of radiofrequency microneedling across the whole face, two weeks apart, at Siriraj Hospital in Bangkok. Straight after each session, one side of the face, chosen at random, received the 0.3% polynucleotide serum and the other side saline, both covered with a clear film for an hour.
/media/body/1: **What a PDRN microneedling session involved.** A numbing cream went on for an hour first. The device then passed over the whole face three times, its needles reaching 0.8–1.5 mm, until the skin turned pink. Each woman had three sessions two weeks apart, so the course took four weeks, and was asked to use an SPF 30 sunscreen daily and keep out of direct sun. Pain averaged 2.2 out of 10, and the team saw no infection, pigment changes, lasting redness or scarring. The serum side reached its significant improvement two months after the last session; at six months, 82% of the women rated each side more than 25% better, and 51% more than 50%.
/media/body/2: The team measured the wrinkles around the eyes with Antera 3D imaging and elasticity with a Cutometer for six months after the last session, and asked each woman to rate her own improvement. Their reasoning: the needles open short-lived channels that let large molecules such as polynucleotides reach deeper. Twenty-nine women completed the study; the paper shows before-and-after photographs of one participant.
/limits/items/0: What was compared. Both sides of every face had the same microneedling; only the serum differed, so the serum side's earlier improvement can be credited to the polynucleotides.
/limits/items/1: Speed, then level. Wrinkle indentation improved significantly by two months on the serum side and by six on the saline side. By then both had improved by a similar amount (10.3 to 8.8, and 11.2 to 9.5): the gain is in speed rather than in the final result.
/limits/items/2: The starting point. The saline side began slightly higher (11.2 against 10.3, not significant). The change within each side, significant at two months with the serum and at six without it, agrees with the between-side test.
/limits/items/3: Depth and elasticity. By six months, elasticity (Cutometer R2) read the same on both sides, 0.58 with the serum and 0.57 with saline. Both ended below their start, and at two months the serum side read lower (0.59 against 0.66); the authors suggest the instrument reads too close to the surface to register deeper change. Maximum wrinkle depth read slightly lower on both sides, with no significant difference at any visit.
/limits/items/4: The women's own view. At six months, 82% rated each side more than 25% improved and 51% more than 50%, with no significant difference between sides (p = 0.189): much of that belongs to the microneedling itself.
/limits/items/5: A clinic procedure. The serum went onto skin just opened by a medical radiofrequency device and stayed under a dressing for an hour. The result belongs to that setting, not to a leave-on serum on intact skin or to microneedling at home.
/limits/items/6: Scale and funding. 29 women at one hospital, followed for six months. The hospital funded the trial; companies provided the device, the medications and the journal fee.
/context/heading: Where this trial sits in the evidence
/context/body/0: Most research on PDRN and polynucleotides concerns injections. This trial belongs to a second group, applied straight after a skin procedure; a 2026 systematic review found PDRN trials mostly injected or procedure-assisted, and small ([Alhussain et al., 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42572627/)).
/context/body/1: The paper calls its ingredient polynucleotides and does not state where they come from. Its 65–130 kDa fragments sit well under the 1,500 kDa line a 2025 review proposes for the name PDRN, and the review notes that the two terms are used interchangeably ([Marques et al., 2025](https://doi.org/10.3390/biom15010148)).
/context/body/2: On intact skin, without needles, the evidence is a different trial: in 31 women, a 0.1% PDRN eye cream reduced crow's-feet wrinkle area and number by up to 23% in 28 days, more than twice the change with 0.1% retinol ([Ye et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350905)), appraised on [its own page](https://www.skingenetix.com/blogs/clinical-studies/pdrn-vs-retinol-split-face-trial-ye-2026). Every study we rely on, graded, is on the [PDRN evidence hub](https://www.skingenetix.com/pages/pdrn-research), alongside our other [ingredient research](https://www.skingenetix.com/pages/the-science).
/faq/questions/0: Does this trial prove the ingredient works?
/faq/questions/1: What concentration did the study use?
/faq/questions/3: Do Skingenetix products reproduce this result?
/faq/answers/0: It shows that PDRN-type polynucleotides brought the result of microneedling forward: after the same radiofrequency microneedling on both sides, wrinkle indentation around the eyes improved significantly within two months on the 0.3% polynucleotide side (between-side p = 0.006), against six months with saline. It is one trial of 29 women; the rest of the evidence is on the [PDRN evidence hub](https://www.skingenetix.com/pages/pdrn-research).
/faq/answers/1: 0.3% polynucleotides of 65–130 kDa (9 mg in each 3 ml vial), with 0.3% hyaluronic acid, amino acids, minerals, vitamins and peptides (REVS NCFS 140HPn, made by Reanzen in Korea). A clinic product, it was applied by the trial team straight after each session and kept under a clear dressing for an hour.
/faq/answers/2: It was run at Siriraj Hospital, Mahidol University, in Bangkok, funded by the hospital's Faculty of Medicine and publicly registered (TCTR20201105007). Companies provided the device and the medications and paid the journal's fee, and the authors declared nothing to disclose.
/faq/answers/3: No. Our [PDRN 1% Renewal Serum](https://www.skingenetix.com/products/pdrn-renewal-serum) contains 1% salmon PDRN and is made for everyday use on intact skin; this trial applied a 0.3% polynucleotide clinic serum to skin just opened by radiofrequency microneedling. The route is different, so the trial's result is not our serum's result. Aftercare following any clinic procedure is for your practitioner to advise.
/meaning/heading: What it means for our products
/meaning/body/0: This trial is part of why we take PDRN seriously as an ingredient: with the procedure held equal on both sides of the face, wrinkles around the eyes improved sooner where the polynucleotides went on.
/meaning/body/1: Skingenetix sells PDRN skincare, so we have a commercial interest in this ingredient. Our [PDRN 1% Renewal Serum](https://www.skingenetix.com/products/pdrn-renewal-serum) and [PDRN Collagen Night Cream](https://www.skingenetix.com/products/pdrn-collagen-night-cream) are leave-on products for intact skin, a different use from this clinic protocol, so we cite the trial for the ingredient as studied, not as a result our products have repeated. For PDRN on intact skin, see the [Ye 2026 trial](https://www.skingenetix.com/blogs/clinical-studies/pdrn-vs-retinol-split-face-trial-ye-2026); the rest of the evidence is on the [PDRN research hub](https://www.skingenetix.com/pages/pdrn-research).
